hero.manifesto: I've been a mid-level full stack software developer for a little over five years, and I grew into the technical lead role on my team gradually, earning my teammates' trust day by day. Over these years I've worked on a wide range of projects: legacy system rebuilds, long-term maintenance contracts, CRMs, marketplaces, healthcare apps and corporate portals with applied AI, including a public healthcare system built with TDD and auditing via Spring AOP, and a digital financial platform launched through a controlled rollout. I work with Java, Spring Boot, Node.js, React and TypeScript. Today, my focus is on building full stack applications.

stats.positions: Positions — Junior I to Tech Lead

timeline.title: Advanced SQL
timeline.desc: Advanced data structures, query syntax, and database optimization.

timeline.title: Java Spring Boot / Quarkus
timeline.desc: From fundamentals to advanced Java with Spring Boot and Quarkus for production applications.

timeline.title: Tech Lead
timeline.desc: Today I'm the architectural reference on my team: I take part in defining the stack, design patterns and structure of new systems, in feature development and in technical refinement with clients. I lead three nationwide projects for institutional clients (public healthcare, industry and telecommunications), each with its own business rules and technical challenges — in these systems we use TDD from start to finish and an auditing module built with Spring AOP. I also coordinated, together with the team, the construction of a digital financial platform integrated with CELCOIN: a NestJS backend, Redis caching, a Next.js frontend as a mobile-first PWA and a controlled rollout up to general availability. I led two simultaneous rebuilds of legacy state government systems, modernizing Groovy/Grails applications into React, TypeScript and Java Spring Boot — work that required a lot of reverse engineering, since the original documentation no longer reflected the system running in production. I structured the process of defining REST contracts between teams before each sprint starts, which brings architecture decisions forward and reduces rework. Day to day, I write a bit less code than I used to, because I coordinate more of the process: I refine tasks, run the ceremonies, talk directly with clients about deadlines, deliveries and acceptance testing, review code and keep the environments and CI/CD pipelines running. I also onboard new developers to the team and take part in the company's strategic decisions.

timeline.title: Angular
timeline.desc: Introduction and advanced use of Angular, PrimeNG, and PrimeFaces in production applications.

timeline.title: Ignite React
timeline.desc: Advanced React with Vanilla JS and a focus on optimizing production applications.

timeline.title: Mid-Level Software Developer
timeline.desc: This is where I went from executing to deciding: I architected the company's first rebuild projects, defining the stack and repository structure for teams that would grow over the following years. I worked on the development and rollout of systems for state public hospitals, contributing architecture decisions that helped make the project viable, and expanded my work to Angular on a nationwide corporate institutional system. I ran technical hiring interviews and started reviewing other developers' code, as well as writing and refining tasks for the team. I saw my work start to split between code and process, with process taking up more and more of my day, and I kept earning the team's trust to take on bigger responsibilities in sprint deliveries. I also worked on smaller internal projects, automating processes that later proved useful for my own management work.

timeline.title: Junior Software Developer III
timeline.desc: I took part in my first architecture definition meetings, still as a contributor, not as a decision-maker. I deepened my knowledge of the stack we used on projects at the time — Java Spring Boot and Quarkus on the backend, React and Angular on the frontend, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB and Redis for databases — aiming to deliver tasks faster without compromising the end result. I started following the full cycle of agile ceremonies — dailies, planning, refinement, reviews and retrospectives — as an active participant, not just someone executing tasks. I also pushed important topics forward in strategic meetings about code review culture and helped put on the table what would later become the REST contracts between development teams.

timeline.title: Junior Software Developer II
timeline.desc: I earned the trust of the more experienced developers and was assigned to a CRM project more complex than usual — a system that was already a success story before I joined. I started taking part in implementing entire features: I integrated LDAP/Active Directory authentication, wrote stored procedures in SQL Server and built reusable React components in TypeScript, always working closely with the Node.js and Java Spring Boot backend. I worked side by side with the QA team on bugs, bugfixes and hotfixes coming straight from production — I tracked down N+1 queries that were freezing entire screens and wrote unit tests to prevent regressions. I also took my first steps in mobile development with React Native, and was already able to show the team and management my potential and my drive to solve problems.

timeline.title: Junior Software Developer I
timeline.desc: I started at the company from the basics, working on one or two projects at a time with simpler tasks: fixing visual bugs, small endpoint adjustments, straightforward CRUDs and specific screens. I joined the daily meetings mostly as a listener, reporting my status to the more experienced developers. I did a lot of pair programming with colleagues who had been there longer — that's how I learned the system's business rules and understood, in practice, what a developer's routine looks like.

timeline.title: GoStack React
timeline.desc: Introduction and deep dive into React for production applications, consolidating fundamental and advanced concepts.

timeline.title: Technical Degree in Information Technology
timeline.desc: Technical program covering programming fundamentals, infrastructure, networking, databases, and front-end/back-end development (RESTful APIs).
